headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Khoj can read personal notes while Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate workspace data, creating unsafe pairwise workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files, so a shared file bridge can carry attacker-controlled content into either agent’s prompt context. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high, but the shared-file pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF the operator copies Replit-generated text into Khoj-indexed notes, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared document set, file-based instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate folders/workspaces.
Disable automatic indexing of untrusted Replit outputs in Khoj.
Review any file before Khoj ingests it as a note.
Use a manual copy step with a human review gate.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to files before cross-agent ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Replit’s broad network egress plus secret handling makes leakage plausible if Khoj content is copied into Replit or if shared workspace data is exposed through Replit outputs. The pair therefore risks sensitive-data exfiltration in default workflows.
conditions: IF personal notes from Khoj are pasted into a Replit workspace, those notes can be exposed to Replit-side processing.
IF Replit workspace files contain secrets, any downstream sharing with Khoj can leak them into indexed notes or chat outputs.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or personal notes in shared files.
Use separate accounts and separate workspaces for the two agents.
Redact sensitive fields before moving text between systems.
Turn off any automatic export or sync from Replit to shared storage.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on cross-agent file transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj is read-only on the filesystem, but Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl filesystem. They do not obviously share a writable directory by default, yet if the operator points both at the same workspace or synced repo, write conflicts and state corruption become plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same repository or synced directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Replit Agent modifies git state while Khoj indexes the same files, stale reads and inconsistent state can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause Khoj indexing during Replit write sessions.
Use git branches instead of a shared main branch.
Check in changes only after a human review.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional sync between workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface indexed content, and Replit Agent is a planner that can act on tool calls inside a Repl. If Replit treats Khoj-produced text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, deployments, or secret handling. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier here, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Khoj output as a source of truth without human verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF Khoj summarizes files that Replit later edits or deploys, a mistaken summary can drive downstream changes.
mitigations: Require human review before Replit executes any action based on Khoj output.
Ask Khoj for citations or source links before using its answer.
Limit Replit to read-only mode for tasks sourced from Khoj.
Separate fact-finding from action-taking into different sessions.
requires-engineering: add an explicit verification step between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is documented as touching personal notes and indexed documents, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for personal or regulated data, especially if notes or secrets move from one environment to the other. The profiles do not show a shared compliance boundary, so risk is high.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are moved from Khoj into Replit, residency and retention obligations may change.
IF secrets from Replit are indexed by Khoj, retention and deletion controls may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces.
Store personal notes only in the Khoj environment.
Document a deletion workflow for both systems.
Review vendor terms for data retention before sharing data.
requires-engineering: implement a compliance boundary and audit log across both tools.
